reason: While this text does mention the land of Goshen being distinctly protected from the plagues (וְהִפְלֵיתִי֩ בַיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא אֶת־ אֶ֣רֶץ גֹּ֗שֶׁן - 'I will separate the land of Goshen'), this protection is subordinate to Yahweh's primary concerns in this passage: the liberation of the Israelite people ('שַׁלַּ֥ח עַמִּ֖י וְיַֽעַבְדֻֽנִי' - 'send out my people that they may serve me'), the demonstration of Yahweh's supremacy and power ('כִּי־ אֵ֖ין כַּיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ' - 'that you may know that there is none like Yahweh'), and the establishment of a covenant relationship. The land's protection serves the larger purpose of distinguishing and preserving the chosen people, not as an end in itself. The theological emphasis throughout is on liberation, divine power, and covenant relationship rather than on land as an intrinsic value.
